newsitem.title: USA: TAG Heuer sees double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: TAG Heuer sees double-digit growth.

text.p: TAG Heuer International SA Chief Executive Christian Viros said on Friday the company expects "very good double-digit growth" in earnings this year after interest and other expenses related to its initial public offering.
Viros, in an interview with Reuters, also said the company would post double-digit growth in revenues in 1996, as well as growth in unit volume.

TAG, a Swiss-based luxury watch maker, sold more than 700,000 watches worldwide in 1995 and recorded revenues of 379.6 million Swiss francs ($314.2 million). The company posted operating income of 76.8 million francs ($63.6 million) and net income of 75.7 million francs ($62.7 million).

Fred Reffsin, president of the company's U.S. unit, said about 150,000 watches were sold in the U.S. in 1995. He said he expects volume to grow three to five percent this year, with revenues up 15 percent.
Viros and other TAG officials were at the New York Stock Exchange on Friday to observe as the company's American Depositary Receipts began trading.
The ADRs were priced at $19.50 and opened up 1/8. After about 10 minutes of heavy trading they were up 1/2 at 20.
